headline: Trump and Warren agree on something: a 10% card cap.
summary: Trump told Fox News on Saturday he would work with the incoming Democratic Congress to cap credit card interest at 10%. The median rate is 22.2%, by the New York Fed's count. He proposed the cap in January; banks fought it and the Republican Congress left it alone. Elizabeth Warren, in line to chair Senate Banking, said yes.
cover_answer: It's their pay for lending. Trump says 22% is too much.
table_question: Should there be a limit on how much extra a lender can ask back?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: The president said this weekend that banks charge grown-ups too much extra when they borrow with a credit card. Borrowing is like taking ten crayons and giving back twelve: the two extra are the bank's pay. He wants that extra smaller, and a senator he usually fights with agrees. Bills are a grown-up job, and the grown-ups have it.
5-7.why: They have seen you tap a card. The crayons make the extra a thing they can count.
5-7.why_long: A seven-year-old reasons from what they have watched, and they have watched you tap a card. The script turns interest into ten crayons paid back as twelve: one countable extra. Who fights is left out; it cannot be counted. Expect 'do we give the bank extra?' Answer, then end as the script does: bills are grown-up work.

8-12.script: Don't pay your card bill in full and the bank charges interest, about 22% a year on a typical card. Trump says he'd work with Democrats to cap that at 10%, and Elizabeth Warren, the Senate's next banking chair, said yes. A cap is a speed limit for banks. Banks say they'd give fewer people cards.
8-12.why: Owe, wait, pay more is a chain. A speed limit is a rule they know; fewer cards is the catch.
8-12.why_long: An eight-year-old is building cause and effect, and this is a chain: owe, wait, pay more, then a rule that stops the last step at 10%. The speed limit they know; fewer cards is the link they will test. Expect 'so is the cap good or bad?' Both are true: $160 billion in interest in 2024, and some people would lose cards.

13-17.script: Who loses if a 10% cap passes? Researchers say Americans would save about $100 billion a year and banks would still profit. Banks say the riskiest borrowers would lose their cards. Second: Trump promised this in 2024 and his party's Congress did nothing, so what changed, apart from who won?
13-17.why: A saving with a cost attached, then a promise with a date on it. Two things to weigh.
13-17.why_long: A sixteen-year-old can hold two true things: a cap saves about $100 billion a year, and banks say the riskiest borrowers lose their cards. Then a timeline: promised in 2024, stalled under his own party, moving as Democrats take Congress. Expect 'so he only means it now?' Ask what would change their mind, then give yours.

5-7.a: It's their pay for lending. Trump says the extra is too big, and he wants a rule to make it smaller.

8-12.a: Rent on borrowed money. $100 at 22% for a year costs $22 extra.

8-12.q: Why don't banks just charge less?
8-12.a: They say the extra pays for people who never pay back.

13-17.q: Who loses if a 10% cap passes?
13-17.a: Banks, and the riskier borrowers they say they'd drop.

13-17.q: Can Trump and Warren actually pass this?
13-17.a: Democrats run Congress from January. Warren is for it; Hawley has a bill.
